q: How much CO2 do anodes add per tonne of aluminium at a Jharsuguda smelter?
title: Jharsuguda smelters: anode CO2 per tonne
short: Prebaked anodes are consumed in the pot, and their carbon leaves as CO2. Multiply net anode consumption per tonne of aluminium by its carbon content and 44/12. The IPCC Tier 1 default for prebake cells is 1.6 t CO2 per tonne of aluminium.
audience: Primary aluminium smelters in Jharsuguda and elsewhere in Odisha using prebaked anode technology

p: Net anode consumption per tonne of aluminium, times carbon content from anode analysis, less sulphur and ash, times 44/12. Use your own plant data for a Tier 2 or Tier 3 figure.
Fuel burnt in the anode baking furnace and pitch volatiles are direct emissions too, if the carbon plant is inside your installation.
Anode CO2 and PFCs from anode effects are the main direct emissions charged for unwrought aluminium. Captive power CO2 is not charged for aluminium today.

example.title: Illustrative anode CO2 for one tonne of aluminium
lines: Net anode consumption: 420 kg per tonne at 97% carbon
CO2: 420 x 0.97 x 44/12 = 1,494 kg, about 1.5 t CO2 per tonne
example.note: Consumption and carbon content are illustrative; compare with the IPCC Tier 1 default of 1.6 t CO2 per tonne for prebake cells.
